brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A Sichuan black tea from the Cuiping district of Yibin, made in two forms: a finely picked gongfu tea and a broken-leaf tea rolled and cut into even granules.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: Local accounts say the gongfu tea was well regarded in London and other markets by the 1950s and took a gold medal at a world food award in 1985, while the broken tea took a silver at the same contest in 1986. They also describe it as the largest and steadiest export among Yibin's goods from 1952 to 1985. These claims come from a single regional account.
processing: Typical of black tea: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: The gongfu tea is picked early in the season and very tender.
appearance_dry: Gongfu: tight, fine, glossy dark strips. Broken: tight, even granules.
taste_profile: Fresh aroma and a mellow, thick taste.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
